_comment: Carry destination for R9-EG-A3 (#1776, parameter objects), from R9-EG-B1 (#1736, the per-solve record).
The round-9 roster's R9-EG-A3 group brief on handoff/audit-r9-fixplan states the baseline this carry corrects; the roster is not on main,
so this file is the in-tree destination. While the two disagree the newer one is right: this one. Shape: .claude/rules/finding-propagation.md.

carries.from: the pull request for R9-EG-B1 (#1736), which moved HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize onto the keyword-only SolveInputs record
carries.control: Measured with the in-tree score, python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff 9fed34071 at the EG-B1 head: params_over_10 28 -> 27, the only function over ten parameters whose arguments were the solve's inputs being optimize. The score's own null control is a tree against itself, which tests/arch_score_head.py pins as NULL.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust the figure: re-run the score at your own merge base, and list the functions over ten parameters with the counting rule metrics/footprint.params_over_10 uses.
carries.brief: The brief's 'about 22 after EG-B1' baseline is not what EG-B1 delivered: the count after it is 27. What remains are model, planner, tariff and flow internals (the physics steps, the DHW planner's helpers, _build_result, _tighten_buffer_caps, _repair_throttled_buffer_caps, the peak cost functions), whose arguments are not the solve's inputs, so EG-A3's parameter objects are its own work and not a follow-on of the solve record. A target stated as a count must be re-derived from 27, and a split that only moves parameters into a pass-through object is red-team move 11, not progress.
